why_this_lane_next: BrowserGym is the best first live-environment lane after ADP because it already exposes a Gymnasium environment with reset, step, observation_space, action_space, reward, termination, and task validate hooks.

relationship_to_adp_lane.difference: ADP normalizes existing traces; BrowserGym lets us run an agent against a real browser environment and call a verifier.

local_preflight.next_setup_action: Install BrowserGym core dependencies in an isolated environment, then rerun import and MiniWoB registry discovery.

first_slice.goal: Convert and run one deterministic local BrowserGym MiniWoB task through our normalized live gym adapter shape.

normalized_target_shape.task: id, source_repo, source_env_id, instruction, seed, constraints
normalized_target_shape.verifier: validate_entrypoint, reward, success, done, verifier_message, verifier_info
normalized_target_shape.scorecard: success, score_0_to_1, steps, elapsed_time, failure_mode, reproducibility_receipt

known_risks: Playwright Chromium may not be installed in the current environment.
Some BrowserGym benchmark families require external services or datasets; first slice must use the smallest local MiniWoB-style task.
Browser observations can be large; receipts should store hashes/summaries instead of raw screenshots or full DOM by default.
Agent execution must stay disabled until the adapter smoke proves deterministic reset, step, validate, and teardown.
next_actions: Add a BrowserGym adapter smoke script in mystuff or the conference tooling.
Run import and registry discovery for browsergym.core and browsergym.miniwob.
Generate one normalized task spec from a local MiniWoB task.
Execute reset and one controlled action without a model agent.
Call validate and produce a scorecard receipt.
Only after that, run a tiny baseline scripted agent or no-op agent benchmark.
